about: The data model of Stage: every record type and field of blueprint section 5.5, with its plain meaning, kind, allowed values, depth, writer, the step that fills it, and one example. Examples show the syntax; values not drawn from the blueprint's gold content are illustrations, never facts about a user's story. Written by WP1 on 2026-09-28 from the build blueprint of 27 Sep 2026.
divider_line: Below this line: details for the AI and the checker. You never need to read them.

end_line.syntax: END OF FILE | <what the file holds> | <n> records
end_line.example: END OF FILE | Scene 10 shots 130-200 | 8 records
end_line.rule: G9: every file ends with exactly one END line; n counts the file's ### records.

record_heading.syntax: ### <TYPE> <ID> <optional plain title>; singleton types have no ID (### PLAN)

field_line.rule: G4: names are lowercased and spaces and hyphens become underscores (a tidy fix, logged as FORM-13).

note_line.rule: G8: a note attached to the record, kept, not parsed.

empty_words.none: Empty (G7). Allowed for text, id_list and repeatable fields, and for any field whose values or also_allowed include none.
empty_words.open: Undecided, listed as a question (G7). Allowed in any field written by ai or user.
empty_words.auto: Code decides (G7). Allowed only where the field's values include auto.
empty_words.missing_rule: These read as missing (G7), so a required field written this way is FORM-05.

text.syntax: Any words to the end of the line. The three characters space, bar, space ( | ) are not allowed inside, because they separate sub-parts.
text.example: Iona's body admits what her words denied.

word.syntax: One allowed value in lowercase snake_case. Compared ignoring case; spaces and hyphens are read as underscores, so 'medium close-up' is medium_close_up. The field's `values` list the allowed words; a field of kind word without a list takes any one lowercase word.

number.syntax: A number written with digits and an optional decimal point, with no unit letters (units live in the field name). A field with `range` takes only values inside it; `whole: true` means no decimal point.

seconds.syntax: A number of seconds (field names end in _s, or the meaning says seconds).

metres.syntax: A number of metres (field names end in _m).

millimetres.syntax: A number of millimetres of lens focal length on a full-frame camera (field names end in _mm).

dollars.syntax: A number of US dollars (field names end in _usd).

words_per_second.syntax: A number of spoken words per second (field names end in _wps).

id.syntax: One ID whose record type is listed in `id_types` (patterns in section 5.3 and in each record type's id_pattern).

id_list.syntax: IDs separated by commas. A comma inside double quotes does not split the list.

id_range.syntax: A first and last ID joined by two full stops (SC01..SC05), or one ID, or IDs separated by commas. The same form the compile command takes.
id_range.grammar_rule: G5 (range form added by WP1, as used by stage.py compile --scene)

lines.syntax: Line numbers of the numbered story, single or as ranges, separated by commas (402, 449-463); or a quote anchor: one quoted string for one line ("Her eyes open."), or a pair joined by 'to' for a range ("Iona chews it." to "street signs either."). Each quoted string has at least 3 words and must match exactly once in its scope (CITE-02). In chat without a numbered story, anchors are required; stage.py adopt turns them into numbers.

quote.syntax: One double-quoted string of exact story words, found in the story (G12, CITE-03).

story_point.syntax: A moment inside a scene named before its beats exist: the scene ID, a space and a quote anchor (SC24 "She deletes the way home."). From step 7 a beat ID is also accepted. When code resolves a story point at step 7 it appends ' = ' and the beat ID (SC24 "She deletes the way home." = SC24-B05); that ending is code_state, never typed or changed by the AI.

story_point_list.syntax: Story points separated by commas (commas inside quotes do not split).
story_point_list.example: SC10 "Her face changes.", SC13 "You did that."

charge.syntax: A value's charge: ---, --, -, 0, +, ++ or +++. The sign is the direction; the count is the strength.

point.syntax: [x, y] or [x, y, z] in metres, in set-plan coordinates (5.4 rule 7).

size.syntax: [w, d, h]: width, depth and height of a box in metres.

span.syntax: t0-t1: a stretch of time inside a shot, in seconds from the shot's start.

date.grammar_rule: added by WP1 for CHOICE date and model dates

file.syntax: A file name or a path inside the project folder, as plain text.
file.grammar_rule: added by WP1 for picture, previs and take files

text_list.syntax: Names or short phrases separated by commas.

sub_parts.syntax: An item (G6): a first part (the item's main value, usually an ID) followed by named sub-parts, each ' | key: value'. Sub-part keys come from the field's `sub_parts` list, in any order. A field whose `first_part` is null has no first part: its value starts with its first named sub-part. Positional (unnamed) sub-parts are never allowed.
sub_parts.example: CH-IONA.S02 | at: left_third | faces: camera | does: chews, stops, frowns

because_list.syntax: Items separated by commas: the ID of any story record (a scene, value, part, beat, speech, move, setup, sequence, plan, plant, fact, chapter, character, voice, place, thing, text, motif, in-story camera, state, world, style, rule, camera system, camera rule, saved choice, lens exception, look, visual plan, sound plan or ladder: the kind's id_types), line:NNN, or line: "<quote anchor>"; or the single word default, allowed only on a normal shot where REASON-02 finds no departure. The same set in every record (fix list C14). A comma inside double quotes does not split the list.
because_list.example: SC10-B07, SC10-V1, MO-MINT, PR-FLASK, LOC-SAYE-KITCHEN, CR-IONA, line:456
because_list.grammar_rule: G5 and 5.4 rule 3 (kind named by the WP1 review: an id_list would refuse line: items)

reference_list.syntax: IDs and field paths separated by commas. A field path is <ID>.<field> (SC10-SU01.lens_mm); a singleton record and the project are named by their type (PLAN.crisis, PROJECT.frame_shape).
reference_list.grammar_rule: 5.5 CHOICE affects (kind named by the WP1 review: an id_list would refuse field paths)

scene_or_story_point.syntax: A scene ID alone for the whole scene (SC26), or a story point (SC26 "She pushes gently away from the rail."); from step 7 a beat ID is also accepted, and code resolves a story point as for the kind story_point. A field's id_types may add other IDs (MOTIF appearance also takes a shot ID from step 8).
scene_or_story_point.grammar_rule: 5.5 CAMSYS break and MOTIF appearance ('a scene or story point'; kind named by the WP1 review)

element_list.syntax: IDs of the record types in id_types, separated by commas; until step 4 designs the things, a story point (SC10 "the flask") may stand for an element that has no record yet. From step 5 on every item must be an ID.
element_list.grammar_rule: G5 (kind added by the fix list after test run 01, C23)

writers.story: Code, copying from the numbered story. Never typed by the AI (FORM-10).
writers.ai: The AI. Within the allowed values; references must exist; a departure from a default needs a why.
writers.user: Only through a CHOICE whose status is answered or defaulted; the field locks when set. An AI-written value without such a CHOICE is FORM-10.
writers.code_state: Code, stored in the record file (locks, status, resolved story points, counts). The AI may not change it (FORM-10), except a field with chat_writer ai in a project marked code_execution: no.
writers.code_derived: stage.py build only. Computed on every build and never stored in record files; an AI-typed value is dropped with a warning (FORM-10, W). FORM-05 never asks for these fields.

writer_rules: Every field has exactly one writer, or a writer_when list whose conditions pick exactly one writer for any one value (5.2).

chat_writer: ai marks a code_state or story field the AI writes in chat before any code runs; FORM-10 accepts the AI's value only in a project marked code_execution: no, and stage.py adopt re-owns it later, logging each difference as a note (N).
Fields marked stored: false are code_derived and never appear in record files.
A user field is set only through a CHOICE whose status is answered or defaulted; set_by_choice names the fixed CHOICE where there is one.

depths.q: Required from quick depth (and at standard and detailed).
depths.s: Required from standard depth (and at detailed).
depths.f: Required only at detailed depth (the user's word is detailed; 'f' is the stored letter).
depths.m: Required only when its module (add-on) is on; `module` names it.

depth_rules: A field is required when the project's depth (or the scene's depth, if higher) is at or deeper than its `depth`, and its `filled_by_step` is at or before the step checked (FORM-05; --all: every field).
`required_when` names a condition from `conditions`: the field is then required only when the condition holds (the starred s* rows of 5.5).
`required_for_all_at` names a depth at which the condition is dropped and the field is required everywhere ('s* turns; f all').
`depth_when` refines the depth for records meeting a condition (for example the story's own RIGHTS record is required at quick).
A required repeatable field may be written as none (G7) when it has no items.
On SHOT.subject, each sub-part has its own `depth`; `required_when_not` names a condition under which the sub-part is not required (at and faces are projected by code where a set plan exists).
A record type with `required_when` (MOVE, FACT, CARDINAL, MUSIC) is written only when its condition holds; its fields are then required at their depths.

filled_by_step_order.about: filled_by_step is a step number (0-11), a checkpoint letter, or an add-on name. For comparison a checkpoint counts as the step it closes and add-ons come after step 11, in the order of their step files.
filled_by_step_order.note: Checkpoint letters A, P, B, C are the checkpoints; add-ons are written add_on_A (storyboards), add_on_B (grey previews), add_on_C (generation packs) and add_on_D (edit and finishing), so the checkpoint A and add-on A never meet. Checkpoints D and E belong to add-ons B and C.

conditions.source_not_screenplay: PROJECT.source_kind is not screenplay (prose, stage play, treatment, comic or game script, mixed): scenes come from the step outline.
conditions.compressing: The user set a runtime target shorter than the story as written, or the source is prose (step 2 compression plan).
conditions.character_has_cue: The character speaks: code found a cue for it in the story.
conditions.set_plan_exists: The scene's location has a set plan (LOCATION size, object and mark items).
conditions.set_plan_needed: Step 4's rule: the place is used by a shot likely to need previs level 2 or more, a reflection or glass shot, or three or more people in one space.
conditions.turn_beat: The beat's turn is not none.
conditions.turn_or_intense_beat: The beat's turn is not none, or its beat_intensity is 4 or more.
conditions.dialogue_pass_beat: At standard: a turn beat, a beat with a flagged line, a beat where a fact is revealed, a refusal, or a line the plan names. At detailed: every beat.
conditions.mirror_rule_exists: The project has a RULE whose kind is mirror.
conditions.device_rule: This RULE's kind is device (a recurring device in prose).
conditions.fact_mode_needs_record: FACT.mode is suspense, mystery or dramatic_irony (about 5-15 in a film); every fact at detailed.
conditions.fact_element_before_reveal: A FACT's element is in the scene before its reveal (audience_knows_from).
conditions.glass_in_frame: A glass surface is in frame.
conditions.eyeline_set: The subject item has an eyeline.
conditions.subject_moves: The subject moves in the frame.
conditions.later_beat_saves_behaviour: A later beat saves a visible behaviour (for example SC13's "Now he looks at her.").
conditions.match_cut_or_continuous_action: The join is a match cut or the scene is continuous action.
conditions.cut_is_split: The CUT type is j_cut or l_cut.
conditions.cut_has_black: The CUT type is cut_to_black, fade or freeze.
conditions.reserved_choice: The value is used under a saved choice (RESERVE).
conditions.framing_critical: The PREVIS record's shot has framing_critical: yes.
conditions.previs_stub: The PREVIS record is a stub code created (status: planned).
conditions.text_in_story: The TEXT words are written in the story.
conditions.depth_detailed: The project's (or the scene's) depth is detailed.
conditions.depth_below_detailed: The project's (or the scene's) depth is quick or standard.
conditions.otherwise: None of the other conditions in the same writer_when list holds.
conditions.when_used: Written only when the thing it records exists (a departure, a flaw, a pov break); the checker never asks for it.
conditions.casting_chosen: Casting (the appearance of the people who play the characters) has been chosen in add-on C.
conditions.filmed_shot: The SHOT kind is not card or black: a camera films it (a title card or black has no setup, height, lens or focus).

common_fields.about: Every record type also takes these three fields (5.5). A record type that lists its own status field (CHOICE, FINDING) uses its own list; status_values on each record type gives the allowed statuses.

fields.name: status
fields.label: Status
fields.meaning: Where the record stands: draft, approved, stale (an input changed) or omitted (cut, keeps its ID).
fields.note_values: CHOICE (open, answered, defaulted), FINDING (open, fixed, accepted) keep their own lists; PREVIS stubs add planned; a VOICE stays draft while place and accents are undecided (5.4 rule 10).

fields.name: locked
fields.label: Locked
fields.meaning: Set when the user approves the record; a locked record gains fields but never silently changes (5.4 rule 5).

fields.name: note
fields.label: Note
fields.meaning: A free note on the record, for people.
fields.example: Staging assumed: the story does not say where Eli stands.
fields.writer_note: ai or user; the user's notes come through the AI

CLIP.syntax: shot ID, a full stop and one digit; or, for a route's clip book, scene ID, -CL and two digits
CLIP.shown_to_user_as: shot 150, clip 1; or clip 3 of the scene

id_rules: IDs never change and are never reused; a cut record keeps its ID with status: omitted (5.3).

Code issues scene, chapter and speech IDs when reading the story, and pre-issues a block for everything else in each handout; named IDs (CH-, LOC-, ...) are formed by the AI from the pattern and checked (FORM-02, ID-02).

An ID exists when it is a record ID in some record file (G10 merges across files), an ID declared by a defines_id field, a speech in speeches.json, a clip ID derived by code, or a PREVIS stub with status: planned (5.4 rule 2).
id_types lists the record types (or other_ids) an ID field accepts; '*' accepts any ID.
Scene IDs have 2 digits, or 3 when the project has more than 99 scenes, fixed per project (ID-09).
Shot numbers go in tens; an insert takes a number between; 990-999 are end cards and black (ID-03).

A field path is <ID>.<field>. Singleton records (PLAN, STYLE, WORLD, CAMSYS, SOUNDPLAN, LADDER) and the project are named by their type: PLAN.crisis, PROJECT.frame_shape (CHOICE affects and sets; SETVALUE target takes the bare type name).

key_glossary.about: What each key on a record type, field, first part or sub-part means, so every reader of this file reads it the same way.

record_type.plain_name: the record type in plain words
record_type.singleton: true when the type has no ID (### PLAN)
record_type.shown_to_user_as: how the ID appears in anything the user reads
record_type.files: the record files it lives in (2.6)
record_type.designed_by_step: the step that designs the type; the default filled_by_step of its fields
record_type.depth: the shallowest depth at which records of this type are written
record_type.status_values: the allowed values of its status
record_type.required_when / required_for_all_at / de: as on fields, for whole records
record_type.accepts_fields_of_target: SETVALUE only: its other field lines are checked against the target's record type
record_type.why_defaults: SHOT only: the defaults of the fields that need a why when they differ (5.4 rule 11)
record_type.field_groups: SCENE only: which file each part_of group lives in

field.name: the field name (lowercase snake_case)
field.label: the plain label views and the book show
field.values: the allowed values (kind word, word_list or number)
field.also_allowed: extra words the field accepts beside its kind (none, all, as_written, default ...) An entry in angle brackets names a form rather than a word: <ID> accepts any existing ID; <scene>-MASTER accepts a scene's master previs (SC06-MASTER).
field.repeat: true when the field appears once per item (G6)
field.first_part: kind sub_parts: the item's first part; null when the item has none
field.defines_id: true when the first part declares an ID (5.3)
field.id_types: record types (or other_ids) an id, id_list or id_range accepts; '*' accepts any
field.pattern: a regular expression the whole value must match
field.range: the lowest and highest allowed number
field.whole: true when the number has no decimal point
field.default: the value that needs no why (5.4 rule 11) or that code assumes
field.reserved_values: values allowed only under a saved choice
field.depth: q, s, f, m or o (depths)
field.depth_note: how the depth applies to items
field.depth_when: a deeper or shallower depth for records meeting a condition
field.required_when: a key of conditions: required only when it holds
field.required_for_all_at: the depth at which required_when is dropped
field.required_note: the requirement in words when it depends on other fields
field.module: the add-on that switches the field on (depth m)
field.writer_when: a list of {when, writer}; exactly one condition holds for any one value
field.writer_note: how the writer rule works in practice
field.chat_writer: ai when the AI writes this field in chat before code runs
field.chat_note: what the AI writes in chat
field.set_by_choice: the fixed CHOICE that sets this user field
field.filled_by_step: the step, checkpoint or add-on that fills it (filled_by_step_order)
field.step_note: when the step depends on the source
field.example: one example value (syntax, not a fact about any story)
field.stored: false for code_derived fields, never in record files
field.part_of: SCENE: list, plan, design or derived
field.one_of: the field or this one must be present
field.copied_from: the field code copies the value from
field.fixed_value: the only value the field takes
field.renamed_from: the 5.5 name, where WP1 renamed the field to avoid a clash (see the build log)
field.added_by: a field WP1 added to 5.5's list (see the build log)

sub_part.depth: for SHOT.subject: the depth from which the sub-part is required
sub_part.required_when_not: a key of conditions under which the sub-part is not required

fields.name: source_kind
fields.label: Kind of story

fields.name: source_format
fields.label: File format

fields.name: language
fields.label: Language

fields.name: genre

fields.meaning: The join out of the scene as the story writes it; a plain cut otherwise.

fields.name: presentation
fields.label: Presentation
fields.meaning: How the scene is shown.

fields.name: host
fields.label: Host
fields.meaning: The device showing the scene when it is on a screen or a recording; written at step 4 by the unit that designs the in-story cameras (fix list C21).

fields.name: event
fields.label: Event
fields.meaning: What changes in the scene, one past-tense sentence with no psychology.
fields.example: Saye proved to Iona with a mint leaf that the three of them had turned and the world had not, and kept them all in her kitchen.

fields.name: sequence
fields.label: Group of scenes
fields.meaning: The group of scenes it belongs to.

fields.name: scene_intensity
fields.label: Scene intensity
fields.meaning: Pressure across the whole film, 1 to 10; exactly one 10 (or one 10 range) on the climax.

fields.name: whose_scene
fields.label: Whose scene
fields.meaning: Whose point of view the scene holds.

fields.name: story_day
fields.label: Story day
fields.meaning: Which day or night of the story (D1, N1 ...); a night takes the number of the day before it (N1 follows D1).

fields.name: rhythm_class
fields.label: Rhythm class
fields.meaning: The scene's pace class, used only by the estimate, never as a design target.

fields.name: tone
fields.label: Tone
fields.meaning: The scene's main tone (D10 §2.1).

fields.name: tone_undercurrent
fields.label: Tone undercurrent
fields.meaning: An optional second tone carried by lines and acting, never by the camera (D10 TN1).

fields.name: tags
fields.label: Tags
fields.meaning: Situations that load situation cards.

fields.name: depth
fields.label: Scene depth
fields.meaning: A depth for this scene above the project's ('Go deeper on scene 13'), logged as a CHOICE.

fields.name: target_duration_s
fields.label: Planned length in seconds
fields.meaning: Planned seconds: the first estimate, then the plan.

fields.name: keep
fields.label: Keep
fields.meaning: Compression decision for the scene.

fields.name: merged_into
fields.label: Merged into
fields.meaning: Where a merged or folded scene went.

fields.name: from_lines
fields.label: Source lines
fields.meaning: Prose: the source passage the scene is drawn from.

fields.name: five_test
fields.label: Five tests
fields.meaning: Prose: A3's five tests as five digits 0 or 1.

fields.name: cardinal
fields.label: Events it carries
fields.meaning: Prose: cardinal events the scene carries.

fields.name: strands
fields.label: Strands
fields.meaning: Prose: strands the scene carries.

fields.name: origin
fields.label: Origin
fields.meaning: Whether the scene is in the story, inferred from it, or invented (authoring mode).

fields.name: location
fields.label: Place
fields.meaning: The place.

fields.name: sub_area
fields.label: Part of the place
fields.meaning: The part of the place used.
fields.example: the table end by the window

fields.name: look
fields.label: Look
fields.meaning: The place-and-time look.

fields.name: value
fields.label: Value
fields.meaning: A value the scene turns; the first part declares the value ID.
fields.example: SC10-V1 | name: normal or altered | core: yes | open: + | close: --- | turns_at: SC10-B07 | kind: revelation
fields.depth_note: At quick only the core value (core: yes) is required; the others from standard.

sub_parts.meaning: Whether it is the scene's core value.
The charge at the scene's start.
The charge at the scene's end.

fields.name: want
fields.label: Want
fields.meaning: What each character wants here, and what they hide or hold back.
fields.example: CH-SAYE | want: to prove the world is mirrored | hidden: she has waited years | holds_back: her own fear

sub_parts.meaning: What they want in this scene, as 'to ...'.

fields.name: driver
fields.label: Driver
fields.meaning: Who drives the scene.

fields.name: conflict
fields.label: Conflict
fields.meaning: The kind of conflict (A2).

fields.name: third_thing
fields.label: Third thing
fields.meaning: What the characters fight through.

fields.name: staging
fields.label: Staging
fields.meaning: One line placing everyone, with 2 to 4 named stations in a scene over 8 beats; 'staging assumed' when the story is silent.
fields.example: Saye at the stove end, Iona across the table at her mark, Eli deep by the back door; stations: door, table, stove.

fields.name: start
fields.label: Start
fields.meaning: Where each character stands at the scene's start.
fields.example: CH-IONA | at: IONA_MARK | faces: CH-SAYE | posture: standing

sub_parts.meaning: A set-plan mark NAME or a point [x, y].
An ID or a point the character faces.

fields.name: scene_idea
fields.label: Scene idea
fields.meaning: The scene in one sentence as a director sees it, naming the at most two departments that change at the main turn.
fields.example: A kitchen that is almost right; at the turn only the camera (the scene's closest frame) and the sound (room sound only) change.

fields.name: department_idea
fields.label: Department idea
fields.meaning: One idea for each department; holding the baseline is a full answer.
fields.example: light | idea: Iona's lamp is the only warm source; it goes down on the table before the hands | because: LK-SAYE-KITCHEN-NIGHT

sub_parts.meaning: yes when the department holds the baseline (written instead of an idea).

fields.name: turn_picture
fields.label: Turn picture
fields.meaning: The frame each turn must show, written as one sentence before any shot.
fields.example: SC10-B07 | picture: Iona close, eyes on Saye just off the lens, her mouth stopped mid-chew

fields.name: dial
fields.label: Dial
fields.meaning: Per beat, how close and how loud: planned size, distance and height, drawn toward the turn.
fields.example: SC10-B07 | size: close_up | distance_m: 1.2 | height: eye:CH-IONA | light: as_look | sound: room_sound

sub_parts.meaning: Planned camera height, as SHOT height.
sub_parts.syntax: eye:CH-ID, seated:CH-ID, kneeling:CH-ID, floor or metres

sub_parts.meaning: as_look, or a change a story source can make (B2 R10), or the rupture.
room_sound, or a change a story source can make, or the rupture.

fields.name: coverage
fields.label: Coverage
fields.meaning: How the scene is covered.

fields.name: rhythm_shape
fields.label: Rhythm shape
fields.meaning: The shape of the cutting.

fields.name: target_asl_s
fields.label: Target average shot length in seconds
fields.meaning: Target average shot length, set from the rhythm shape, the tone and card 13, never from rhythm_class.

fields.name: rupture
fields.label: Rupture
fields.meaning: The one break in the scene's pattern.
fields.example: SC10-B07 | device: hold | breaks: the cutting between singles

fields.name: tone_shift
fields.label: Tone shift
fields.meaning: A change of tone inside the scene, on a turn or a drop (D10 TN2), or none.

first_part.meaning: The beat where the tone shifts.

sub_parts.meaning: The one visible system that changes.

fields.name: room_sound
fields.label: Room sound
fields.meaning: The steady background sound here.

fields.name: geography
fields.label: Geography
fields.meaning: Action scenes: where everything is (card 15, D11).
fields.example: the shaft runs north-south; the cage hangs at the third landing

fields.name: cause_chain
fields.label: Cause chain
fields.meaning: Action scenes: each cause and its effect.
fields.example: the brake bolts are gone; the cage drops; the cable snaps taut

fields.name: escalation
fields.label: Escalation
fields.meaning: Action scenes: how the danger grows.
fields.example: from a slip, to a fall, to a shot

fields.name: reversal
fields.label: Reversal
fields.meaning: Action scenes: the beats where the advantage changes hands.

fields.name: action_score
fields.label: Action score
fields.meaning: Action scenes: a text block, one row per count, one column per body, the set and the camera.
fields.example: see the table above the divider
fields.syntax: text; the block itself may sit in the plain part and be referred to here

fields.name: time_treatment
fields.label: Time treatment
fields.meaning: Action scenes: how screen time relates to story time (slow_motion only where the camera system allows it).

fields.name: departure
fields.label: Departure
fields.meaning: A scene-level break from a film rule.
fields.example: CAMSYS | what: one handheld shot as Iona loses control of the car | why: "A night bus comes at them with its number written backwards." is the beat control is lost (B1 R17)

sub_parts.meaning: Why, quoting a line, naming an object or action, or citing an ID.

fields.name: additions
fields.label: Additions
fields.meaning: Inventions awaiting keep or cut, each marked whether it changes what the scene means.
fields.example: Iona sets the lamp down before the raised hands | changes_meaning: yes

first_part.meaning: What was added, or its ID.

sub_parts.meaning: yes for a new object, or a new move at a turn.

fields.name: lines_not_shown
fields.label: Lines no shot shows
fields.meaning: Story lines of the scene that no shot (no list item at quick) shows on purpose, each with its reason, so COVER-02 is silent for them.
fields.example: 486 | why: the transition "CUT TO BLACK." is the cut SC10-C200, not a shot

fields.name: flags
fields.label: Flags
fields.meaning: Scene-level faults found, never fixed (line-level faults are BEAT flag).

fields.name: era
fields.label: Era
fields.meaning: The mirror era the scene is in (from the mirror RULE's era lines).

fields.name: frame_handedness
fields.label: Frame handedness
fields.meaning: Whether the scene's frame is original or reversed.

fields.name: switch_at
fields.label: Switch at
fields.meaning: The line where the era switches inside the scene.

fields.name: states_in_play
fields.label: States in play
fields.meaning: The element states valid in the scene.

fields.name: duration_est_s
fields.label: Estimated length in seconds
fields.meaning: Estimated scene length from its shots.

fields.name: label
fields.label: Label
fields.meaning: The scene's plain name in views (Scene 10 - Saye's kitchen).

fields.name: eighths
fields.label: Length in eighths of a page
fields.meaning: The scene's length on the page in eighths (5.6 labels and counts).

PART.meaning: A part of a scene with its own turn.

fields.name: beats
fields.label: Beats
fields.meaning: The beats in the part.

fields.name: turn
fields.label: Turn
fields.meaning: The part's turn beat.

fields.name: starts
fields.label: How it starts
fields.meaning: How the part starts.

fields.name: lines
fields.label: Lines
fields.meaning: The story lines the beat covers.

fields.name: action
fields.label: Action
fields.meaning: Who does what, as a tactic (an -ing word).

sub_parts.meaning: What the act does to the other person, as an -ing word.

fields.name: reaction
fields.label: Reaction
fields.meaning: Who reacts, as a tactic.

fields.name: task
fields.label: Task
fields.meaning: What the hands do.

sub_parts.meaning: The visible task, with no emotion words (WORDS-01).

fields.name: beat_intensity
fields.label: Beat intensity
fields.meaning: Pressure inside the scene, 1 to 5 (at most two 5s per part).

fields.name: turn
fields.label: Turn
fields.meaning: Whether a value turns here.

fields.name: turn_kind
fields.label: Turn kind
fields.meaning: How the value turns.

fields.name: charge
fields.label: Charge
fields.meaning: Each value's charge after the beat.

fields.name: flag
fields.label: Flag
fields.meaning: A flaw in one line, flagged, never fixed (A1).

fields.name: engaged_pair
fields.label: Engaged pair
fields.meaning: In a three-person scene, the two engaged (B3 R25, A1 R5).

fields.name: silent_third
fields.label: Silent third
fields.meaning: In a three-person scene, the witness; none for a beat where nobody is left to witness.

fields.name: five_steps
fields.label: Five steps
fields.meaning: Desire, obstacle, choice, action, expression as visible moments (five items).
fields.example: choice | shows: she takes the leaf from Saye's fingers

fields.name: landing_face
fields.label: Landing face
fields.meaning: Who the audience watches when the line lands.
fields.syntax: a character ID, insert:<ID>, or wide

fields.name: unsaid
fields.label: Unsaid
fields.meaning: What a character thinks and does not say.
fields.example: CH-IONA | thought: then we are not home

fields.name: carrier
fields.label: Carrier
fields.meaning: What makes the unsaid seen or heard (an ID, or words).

fields.name: pause_after
fields.label: Pause after
fields.meaning: The pause after the beat, by tier (constant pause_tiers); a hold above 4.0 s needs a saved choice.
fields.example: long | seconds: 3 | picture: hold | sound: room sound only

sub_parts.meaning: The pause's length, inside its tier.
What the picture does in the pause.
What is heard in the pause.

fields.name: emphasis
fields.label: Emphasis
fields.meaning: How loud each motif or thing is on this beat, 0 to 3.

fields.name: added_emphasis
fields.label: Added emphasis
fields.meaning: An extra signal on this beat: 0 or 1, and what it is (0 where the script marks the beat).

fields.name: change
fields.label: Change
fields.meaning: The configuration change on a turn.
fields.example: Iona steps back from the table; Saye does not move.

fields.name: distance
fields.label: Distance
fields.meaning: Detailed staging: the distance and zone between two characters.

fields.name: core_word
fields.label: Core word
fields.meaning: Detailed dialogue: the word carrying the line's meaning.

fields.name: cut_rule
fields.label: Cut rule
fields.meaning: Detailed dialogue: how the cut treats the line.

fields.name: fact
fields.label: Fact
fields.meaning: Detailed: facts revealed or protected on this beat.

fields.name: script_marked
fields.label: Marked by the script
fields.meaning: yes when the beat's lines already mark it: a capitalised sound, emphasis or text token, or a light, colour or darkness word that stage.py read found and that is light in its sentence, not a person's colour (B1 P11, B4 R17). CRAFT-10 and added_emphasis_per_beat_max read it.

SPEECH.id_syntax: scene ID, -D and 2 digits (3 if a scene has more than 99), numbered in cue order within the scene

fields.name: speaker
fields.label: Speaker
fields.meaning: Who speaks.

fields.name: line
fields.label: Line number
fields.meaning: The line number of the cue (a quote anchor in chat).

fields.name: text
fields.label: Words
fields.meaning: The exact words spoken.

fields.name: parenthetical
fields.label: Parenthetical
fields.meaning: The parenthetical, if any.

fields.name: extension
fields.label: Cue extension
fields.meaning: The cue extension, if any ((V.O.), (O.S.)).

fields.name: path
fields.label: Path
fields.meaning: How the voice reaches us.

fields.name: origin
fields.label: Origin
fields.meaning: Whether the words are the story's, adapted, or invented.

fields.name: word_count
fields.label: Words
fields.meaning: The number of words in the speech, read by the time floor and the captions (5.6).

MOVE.meaning: A character's move on the set plan (never a camera move).

fields.name: beat
fields.label: Beat
fields.meaning: The beat it happens in.

fields.name: who
fields.label: Who
fields.meaning: The character who moves.

fields.name: from
fields.label: From
fields.meaning: Where the move starts: a mark or a point.

fields.name: to
fields.label: To
fields.meaning: Where the move ends: a mark or a point.

fields.name: via
fields.label: Via
fields.meaning: A mark or a point the path passes through, or none when the move goes straight; a change of height is a posture change, not a via.

fields.name: start_s
fields.label: Start in seconds
fields.meaning: When it starts, counted from the start of the first shot that shows its beat.

fields.name: dur_s
fields.label: Length in seconds
fields.meaning: How long the move takes.

fields.name: faces
fields.label: Faces
fields.meaning: What the character faces at the end: an ID or a point.

fields.name: posture
fields.label: Posture
fields.meaning: The posture at the end.

fields.name: why
fields.label: Why
fields.meaning: The want or task behind the move (toward the door = escape).
fields.example: to set the lamp down where Saye can see her hands

fields.name: origin
fields.label: Origin
fields.meaning: Whether the move is in the story, inferred, or invented.

SETUP.meaning: A camera position in a scene (shown to the user as camera A, B, C ... in order).

fields.name: at
fields.label: Position
fields.meaning: The camera position as a point (with a set plan).

fields.name: at_words
fields.label: Position in words
fields.meaning: The camera position in words (without a set plan).

fields.name: look_at
fields.label: Aimed at
fields.meaning: The point the camera aims at.

fields.name: look_at_words
fields.label: Looks at, in words
fields.meaning: Where the camera aims, in words (without a set plan).

fields.name: lens_mm
fields.label: Lens in millimetres
fields.meaning: The lens (full-frame).

fields.name: use
fields.label: Use
fields.meaning: What the setup is for.
fields.example: the reflection two-shot through the wild wall

fields.name: side
fields.label: Side of the line
fields.meaning: Which side of the line the camera is on.

fields.name: mount
fields.label: Mount
fields.meaning: What the camera is fixed to: the world, or an ID of a moving thing.

SHOTLIST.meaning: The one-line shot list that fixes the shot IDs and count before detail is written.

fields.name: item
fields.label: Shot
fields.meaning: One planned shot; the first part declares the shot ID. At quick the items are the final shots.
fields.example: SC10-SH150 | beats: SC10-B07, SC10-B08 | role: turn | size: close_up | frame: single | subject: CH-IONA | time: 15 | shows: Iona chews, stops, chews once more; "Not mint."; we stay on her through Saye's answer

first_part.meaning: The shot ID it declares, from the issued block, in tens.

sub_parts.meaning: How much the scene depends on it.
Who is in frame: character or state IDs.
One line of what we see.

fields.name: approved
fields.label: Approved
fields.meaning: The user passed checkpoint C, or it was reported without changes.

SHOT.meaning: One shot, written from its list item at standard and detailed, reason-first (purpose and because before camera values).
SHOT.id_syntax: scene ID, -SH and 3 digits in steps of 10; an insert takes a number between (SH155); 990-999 for end cards and black

why_defaults.height: the eye of the whose_scene character, or of the subject

SHOT.why_note: size and frame never need a why (the dial and the list carry their reasons); turn shots always carry a why (5.4 rule 11).

fields.name: beats
fields.label: Beats
fields.meaning: The beats the shot shows.

fields.name: lines
fields.label: Lines
fields.meaning: The story lines the shot shows (a quote anchor pair in chat).

fields.name: purpose
fields.label: Purpose
fields.meaning: What the audience must get from the shot, one sentence.
fields.example: Iona's body admits what her words denied; Saye's proof lands on her face.

fields.name: because
fields.label: Because
fields.meaning: The records that justify the shot (5.4 rule 3), or default on a normal shot with no departure.
fields.syntax: IDs, line:NNN or line: "<quote anchor>", or default

fields.name: role
fields.label: Role
fields.meaning: How much the scene depends on the shot.

fields.name: kind
fields.label: Kind of shot
fields.meaning: The kind of shot: live (filmed in the scene), insert (a thing close), pov (what a character sees with their own eyes), screen (the picture an in-story camera or device makes, at that camera's own lens; CRAFT-07), card (a title) or black.

fields.name: why
fields.label: Why
fields.meaning: The story reason for any value on the list in 5.4 rule 11 that departs from its default, or for any departure from the camera system; always on turn shots. One sentence quoting a line, naming an object or action, or citing an ID.

fields.required_note: Required on turn shots and on every departure (REASON-02).

fields.name: origin
fields.label: Origin
fields.meaning: Where the shot's content comes from.

fields.name: additions
fields.label: Additions
fields.meaning: Inventions in frame (each also listed in the scene's additions).
fields.syntax: IDs separated by commas, or text

fields.name: pov_break
fields.label: Point-of-view break
fields.meaning: Why the shot leaves the whose-scene character's place or knowledge (A3 rule 37).

fields.name: setup
fields.label: Setup
fields.meaning: The camera position.

fields.name: frame
fields.label: Frame
fields.meaning: Who is framed.

fields.name: frame_detail
fields.label: Frame detail
fields.meaning: Framing variant (standard when the framing is a saved choice; every shot at detailed).

fields.name: size
fields.label: Shot size
fields.meaning: Shot size.

fields.name: angle
fields.label: Angle
fields.meaning: Tilt of the camera (dutch only when a saved choice allows it).

fields.name: height
fields.label: Camera height

fields.syntax: eye:CH-ID, seated:CH-ID, kneeling:CH-ID, floor, or metres
fields.default: the eye of the whose_scene character, or of the subject

fields.name: lens_mm

fields.meaning: The lens (full-frame).

fields.name: focus

fields.meaning: Depth of field.

fields.name: focus_on

fields.name: move
fields.label: Camera move

fields.name: move_reason
fields.label: Cause of the camera move
fields.meaning: What causes the camera move.

fields.name: mount
fields.label: Mount
fields.meaning: What the camera is fixed to.

fields.name: stance
fields.label: Camera stance
fields.meaning: The camera's stance.

fields.name: dominant
fields.label: Seen first
fields.meaning: What is seen first. At detailed the AI writes it; at standard code derives it from focus_on, role and the first subject.

fields.name: placement
fields.label: Placement
fields.meaning: Where the dominant sits.

fields.name: layers
fields.label: Layers
fields.meaning: Foreground, middle and background.

fields.name: frame_in_frame
fields.label: Frame within the frame
fields.meaning: A frame within the frame.

fields.name: device
fields.label: Expressive device
fields.meaning: At most one expressive device.

fields.name: glass
fields.label: Glass
fields.meaning: Every glass surface in frame.
